To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
faceting at grain boundaries can lead to the formation of chemical patterns and that these patterns can influence the mechanical properties of a material.
Faceting occurs at the grain boundaries in a model Al alloy.
faceting at grain boundaries in Al-Zn-Mag-Cu alloys is strongly correlated to the local chemistry, and that this interplay leads to periodic segregation patterns or preferential precipitation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay of chemistry and faceting at grain boundaries in Al alloys.
the influence of the grain boundary structure on its chemical properties.
the interplay of chemistry and faceting at grain boundaries in a model Al alloy, which is of importance to understand and optimize the properties of engineering Al alloys.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the segregation-faceting phenomenon is a common feature of grain boundaries in Al alloys and that the segregation-facet interplay is not a simple one but a complex one, depending on the alloy composition, the grain boundary character and the processing route.
faceting and segregation are coupled and mutually dependent, and that the segregation-faceting coupling leads to the formation and evolution of complex patterns in grain boundaries.
the faceting and segregation interplay is a general phenomenon that can occur in any material and is not limited to the model system investigated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the faceting of a grain boundary in a binary alloy is a result of a competition between the grain boundary energy, the chemical potential of the solute and the solubility limit.
the interplay of chemistry and faceting at grain boundaries in a model Al alloy is a complex process.
segregation-facets co-evolution can occur in real Al alloys and can lead to the formation of segregation-facets patterns.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the local chemical structure of grain boundaries is not only determined by the local crystal structure but also by the chemical environment.
segregation-facetting interplay is not restricted to bicrystals, but also occurs in bulk engineering Al alloy systems, thus affecting their performance.
segregation-faceted interfaces in Al alloys are not a static feature but a dynamic process.
